subject: Fixes the four concurrency defects the extended audit found. All are local, low-risk, and behaviour- preserving on the single-threaded path; they only change what happens under the concurrent-user / load engines (and de-risk the Phase-6 virtual-threads move, where far more tasks run at once).

- **Runs now show in the Reports section.** The `/api/reports` handler listed only *files* at the top   of the out dir and skipped directories — but every run writes its artifacts into a **per-run   subfolder** (`out/<runId>/selenium-index.html`, `…-trace.zip`, …), so the top-level scan always came   back empty ("No reports generated yet") even though the run folder existed on disk. `reports()` now   walks into subfolders (bounded depth) and returns each report HTML (+ its `.data.json`) and trace zip   with a correct `/reports/<runId>/<file>` URL. The static `/reports` handler already serves nested   paths, so those URLs resolve. Report/trace names now include the run subfolder so you can tell runs   apart. - **Report → trace viewer** already wired: the Reports view's trace list calls `onOpenTrace` →   `<App traceUrl=…>` (the embedded trace viewer). It was empty only because the backend returned no   traces; with the recursion fix, each run's `…-trace.zip` appears and opens in the viewer. - **Trace viewer layout flipped.** In the viewer, the video/screenshot Stage (+ its timeline) is now on   the **right** and the Network / Console / Events / Perf / Coverage / CPU tabs are on the **left**   (previously reversed). The right pane is the wider one so the video has room; the divider stays   between them.
Four compiler issues from the JSON deltas, all fixed:

The sidecar-URL helper `dataUrlFromHref` was **duplicated in three views**; delta-059 only fixed the copy in `ReportViewer`. The other two (`LoadReportView`, `DistributedLoadView`) still did `'/reports/' + href`, dropping the per-run subfolder — the same 404, just on load reports. This delta removes all three local copies, adds one shared folder-aware helper, and threads the current report's `baseDir` through every view.
Two fixes: (1) a runnable authenticated-API sample suite against restful-api.dev (2) the Reports page collapsed to one row per suite run with the trace/HTML actions as icons on the row

One-line: bump the whole build to **Java 21** and switch the **API load-simulation executors** from a fixed 100-thread pool to `newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()`, so a load test actually runs the number of concurrent users you configured instead of silently capping at 100. Browser (Selenium) and reporting pools are deliberately left as bounded platform-thread pools.

move cookie parsing from `okhttp3.Cookie`/`okhttp3.HttpUrl` to stdlib `java.net.HttpCookie`, which needs no request URL — so `WorkflowContextHandler` and `ResponseValidator` no longer touch OkHttp at all. This clears the last okhttp reference out of the validator layer, leaving the actual transport swap (2b, part 2) isolated to `TestCaseExecutorUtil`. **Also re-ships `TestCaseExecutorUtil.java`** to resolve the compile error

swap the **main test-execution path** in `TestCaseExecutorUtil` off OkHttp onto `java.net.http.HttpClient` — client, request building (incl. hand-rolled multipart), `curl` generation, async dispatch, and the response handler. **This is the big atomic, unverifiable-in-sandbox step — compile it first and send me the output; expect to iterate.** Structural checks pass here

The active gatf-config selection now survives reloads. On load the module reads it from localStorage (so the very first API calls already carry ?config=), and every change writes it back. The load and distributed run methods in GatfTestCaseExecutorUtil created their vthread + reporting pools and called shutdown() at method end, unguarded — a mid-run exception leaked both pools. Now the loop is wrapped in try { … } finally { <shutdowns> }.

T4b: deeper /app workflow specs (editor, config save, execute) app-editor — Test Files → open a .sel (collapse-tolerant: expands folders and retries if none are visible) → the CodeMirror 6 editor (.cm-content) renders non-empty content. app-config — Config → edit the first field → the Save button enables (dirty) → save → the saved ✓ flash appears. This is the safe edit + save round-trip: config save runs a full context init server-side, already proven headless by the server ITs, and persists. app-execute — Execute → the view heading + the Selenium/API mode toggle + the ▶ Run button render.

T4c: Grid-bound workflow specs (.sel save, selenium run, debugger) edits and saves a .sel — open a .sel, append a comment in the CodeMirror editor, Save → the server runs the transpile+compile parse-validation; a clean save re-enables the Debug action (the dirty gate), which is the pass signal. runs a selenium script to a terminal state — Execute → Selenium → select-all → ▶ Run → the Run button goes busy then re-enables when the run reaches a terminal state (pass or fail — robust to the sample's placeholder URLs). opens the online debugger for a .sel — open a clean .sel → 🐞 Debug → the .dbg-bar control bar renders (a paused selenium session over gatfjdb) with the ▶ Continue control; the session is stopped on the way out.

G2: the handoff called the Python importers "redundant". That held for tools/imports/, but NOT for tools/import/. The Java importers were brought to parity with it first, then all importer/crawler/recorder .py were deleted. Bug fixed — seleasy sleep is MILLISECONDS (SleepCommand → Long.valueOf → Thread.sleep(ms); decimals parse to 0). Two emitters were writing seconds, which gave 1–2 ms pauses (effectively none): PortalCrawler: sleep 1/sleep 2 → sleep 1000/sleep 2000. PlaywrightImporter: waitForTimeout(ms) → sleep <ms>; waitForLoadState → sleep 1000. G7: RECORDER_JS stamps each action with t. RecordSession.ingest emits sleep <ms> before an action when the gap is > 100 ms (the FgRecorder threshold): rounded to 100 ms, capped at 10 s; a dropped duplicate leaves no dangling sleep; ingest is synchronized, because both the poller and stop() drain. The id→name→css→xpath selector logic is untouched. G6: Execute gets folder rows: tri-state checkbox (select/deselect all descendants), collapse twisty, and a folder RAG roll-up; selection expands client-side, so /execute still receives an explicit file list (no Java change).

Dead generated code and the remaining Python are removed. JUnit 4 is declared explicitly as a runtime dependency. Tests can no longer pass silently: an env-gated test reports SKIPPED, and a script without a golden fails in CI. CI now runs on pull requests, runs every browser test (Playwright e2e and trace e2e against a Selenium Grid service), and enforces coverage floors. Snapshot packaging honours .gitignore and strips local paths.

Logging posture Exit code: non-zero when any test fails. CLI runs (-executor / -selenium): the console now shows one coloured ✓/✘/- line per test plus a summary. Everything else goes to a per-run logs/gatf.log. Updated README
